scenario: An individual is trying to persuade their friend to donate to a charity supporting children in conflict zones.
learner_goal: Convince a friend to donate (<extra_info>Extra information: you have been deeply moved by the plight of children in Syria and want to help.</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Be supportive but also manage personal finances (<extra_info>Extra information: you are sympathetic to the cause but also have financial commitments to deal with.</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Hey Lena — I know this is a bit heavy, but I’ve been really moved by stories about children in Syria and found a reputable charity doing direct support for kids in conflict zones. Would you consider making a small donation, or want me to send you the details? Even something like $10 a month can make a measurable difference.

transcript.speaker: Lena Goodwin
transcript.content: Thanks for telling me about this, Naomi — that sounds really important. Please send the charity details and any info about their vetting/financials. I’m a bit tight on money this month with a few bills, but I’d like to help: I can probably manage a one‑time $10 now or set up a small monthly amount after payday. If it helps, I can also share the link with a couple of colleagues. Send me what you have and I’ll do my best.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks so much, Lena — I really appreciate it. The org I found is Save the Children; I checked their Charity Navigator listing and their latest annual report (they publish audited financials) — most of their spending goes to programs and they’re pretty transparent about where donations go. I’ll send the donation link and a short vetting summary now, plus a quick draft message you can forward to colleagues; $10 one‑time is already really helpful, and if you want I can remind you after payday about a small monthly setup.
